This position helps standardize anatomy, improve image quality, and keep the abdominal organs and bowel in a consistent orientation for interpretation.

key_facts: Standard abdominal CT positioning is usually supine.
Arms are often elevated above the head to minimize streak artifact from the upper limbs.
The abdomen is scanned in a neutral position without the patient holding a special posture, unless a specific protocol requires otherwise.
Normal axial CT images show the liver, stomach, pancreas, kidneys, aorta, vertebral body, and bowel loops in expected anatomic positions.
Patient motion or suboptimal positioning can degrade abdominal CT image quality.
